description: "Draw a circular genome plot in the browser — stacked data tracks around a ring with connection ribbons — from one portable spec."
author: "Isaac Neuhaus"

A circular (Circos-style) plot wraps a genome — or any ordered set of segments — into a ring, stacks
several **data tracks** around it, and draws **ribbons** for relationships between positions. Building
one in the browser by hand is serious trigonometry. CanvasXpress is a JavaScript library at heart, so
it's a `tracks × segments` matrix plus a `config`.

## Load the library

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
```

## The markup and the spec

Rows are the tracks you draw, columns are the positions around the ring; `Region` segments the ring,
and `circularConnections` is a list of `[colour, from, to]` ribbons.

```html
<canvas id="circ" width="560" height="560"></canvas>
<script>
  var segments = [], tracks = ["Expression", "Methylation", "CopyNumber", "Density"],
      cols = ["rgb(220,40,40)", "rgb(40,120,220)", "rgb(40,160,60)", "rgb(240,150,20)"];
  for (var i = 0; i < 80; i++) segments.push("s" + (i + 1));
  function pick(a) { return a[Math.floor(Math.random() * a.length)]; }

  var data_m = tracks.map(function () {
    return segments.map(function () { return Math.round((Math.random() * 4 - 2) * 100) / 100; });
  });
  var region = segments.map(function (_, i) { return "chr" + (Math.floor(i / 20) + 1); });
  var conns = [];
  for (var c = 0; c < 18; c++) conns.push([pick(cols), pick(segments), pick(segments)]);

  var data = { y: { vars: tracks, smps: segments, data: data_m }, x: { Region: region } };
  var config = {
    graphType: "Circular",
    circularConnections: conns,
    circularTrackGraphType: ["bar", "heatmap", "line", "dot"],
    circularTrackGraphWeight: [30, 20, 25, 25],
    circularTrackName: [1, 2, 3, 4],
    segregateSamplesBy: ["Region"],
    title: "Circos-style multi-track plot with connections"
  };

  new CanvasXpress("circ", data, config);
</script>
```

## Live result

```{=html}
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
<canvas id="circLive" width="560" height="560"></canvas>
<script>
(function () {
  function draw() {
    if (typeof CanvasXpress === "undefined") { return setTimeout(draw, 60); }
    var segments = [], tracks = ["Expression", "Methylation", "CopyNumber", "Density"],
        cols = ["rgb(220,40,40)", "rgb(40,120,220)", "rgb(40,160,60)", "rgb(240,150,20)"];
    for (var i = 0; i < 80; i++) segments.push("s" + (i + 1));
    function pick(a) { return a[Math.floor(Math.random() * a.length)]; }
    var data_m = tracks.map(function () {
      return segments.map(function () { return Math.round((Math.random() * 4 - 2) * 100) / 100; });
    });
    var region = segments.map(function (_, i) { return "chr" + (Math.floor(i / 20) + 1); });
    var conns = [];
    for (var c = 0; c < 18; c++) conns.push([pick(cols), pick(segments), pick(segments)]);
    new CanvasXpress("circLive",
      { y: { vars: tracks, smps: segments, data: data_m }, x: { Region: region } },
      { graphType: "Circular", circularConnections: conns,
        circularTrackGraphType: ["bar", "heatmap", "line", "dot"],
        circularTrackGraphWeight: [30, 20, 25, 25], circularTrackName: [1, 2, 3, 4],
        segregateSamplesBy: ["Region"], title: "Circos-style multi-track plot with connections" });
  }
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

Each ring is one track; the inner ribbons are the connections. Hover a segment to read its values;
swap the matrix and ribbons for your own genomic tracks and interactions.

## Why "reproducible"

The matrix, the connections and the `config` **are** the figure — one portable JSON spec that renders
the same from R, Python, or a web page.
